nodes.body: `probeHttp()` currently treats every non-5xx response as ready. That makes the new preflight produce false greens whenever the pinned port is occupied by the wrong service but still returns `200`, `301`, or even `404` here. In that state `testenv:status` and the run preflight say the environment is usable, then the real run fails later on task creation or browser navigation. Please tighten this probe to validate the expected success shape for each dependency (for example, require the relay endpoint to return the expected JSON/2xx contract and require OpenChamber to return its real landing page), and add a regression test for the wrong-service-on-port case.

This no longer mirrors the real launcher. `resolveCodeArtsLaunchTarget()` falls back to `codearts` on `PATH` for every non-Windows platform (`integrations/codearts/executable.ts`, lines 18-21), but the preflight only checks `CODEARTS_BIN` or the Windows installer paths. On Linux/macOS a valid `bun run codearts` setup will therefore be reported as `codearts DOWN`, and both `testenv:status` and run preflight will block readiness/acceptance even though the client is actually launchable. Please reuse the same resolution routine as the launcher here, or at least probe `codearts` on `PATH` on non-Windows platforms, with a regression test covering that path-based install.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject non-loopback URLs before managing local ports**

When `GAMEFORGE_RUN_RELAY_URL` or `GAMEFORGE_OPENCHAMBER_URL` contains a non-loopback URL, this function discards the hostname and retains only its port. For example, a supported remote relay URL such as `https://relay.example.com/` makes `testenv:up` start a local service on port 443 while probing and printing the remote URL, and `testenv:down` may kill an unrelated local node/bun listener on port 443. Validate that these management URLs are credential-free loopback HTTP(S) before deriving the local port.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve the tier when rewriting session metadata**

For every run that reaches `UiTestController.run`, this initial write records `tier`, but the controller subsequently calls `recordSession` with a newly constructed `HarnessSession` that has no tier; `FileEvidenceSink.recordSession` overwrites `metadata.json` rather than merging it. Consequently successful readiness and acceptance sessions lose the explicit metadata marker intended to prevent a readiness result from being mistaken for an end-to-end integration verdict, so pass the tier through the controller or avoid the second destructive write.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Treat HTTP error responses as unavailable dependencies**

When either probe endpoint responds with a 4xx status, this branch reports it as available because only 5xx responses are rejected. An unauthenticated Relay returning 401/403 or a wrong service returning 404 can therefore make `testenv:status` claim the environment is ready and let the run preflight pass even though the subsequent Authority or browser operation cannot work; probe with the configured Relay authorization where applicable and require the endpoint's expected successful status.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Cancel startup before resolving a concurrent down**

When `down()` or the CLI's SIGINT handler runs while `up()` is awaiting a port check or service readiness, `#stopAll()` only captures services already present in `#services`; `up()` has no cancellation state and can subsequently spawn the current or next service after that snapshot. The shutdown promise can therefore resolve and `testenv-cli.ts` can exit while a newly spawned Relay or OpenChamber child remains alive, especially when Ctrl+C arrives between the two service startups. Coordinate `down()` with the in-flight `up()` and prevent any further spawn before reporting cleanup complete.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Diagnose the dependency that actually failed preflight**

Every `Preflight failed: ...` message matches this first rule and is diagnosed as an unavailable Authority Relay, even when the only failed dependency is `codearts`, `openchamber-service`, or `openchamber-build`. In those common cases the newly added diagnosis gives a false likely cause and omits the dependency-specific remediation already present in the failure string; classify the named blocking dependency instead of assigning all preflight failures to Relay.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Match the timestamped GUI screenshot evidence**

The Playwright driver writes screenshots as `gui/<timestamp>-failed.png` and `gui/<timestamp>-success.png`, but diagnosis filters candidates by exact membership and these fixed paths are never produced. A GUI-diagnostics failure therefore omits the relevant failed/success screenshot from both terminal and Markdown guidance even though it exists on disk; match the label suffix or derive paths from `browser-report.ndjson` instead.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate the failure hold before preparing evidence**

The CLI accepts any positive `--failure-hold-ms`, while the controller rejects values above 300000 before entering its guarded run/finalization path. In a headed run with, for example, `--failure-hold-ms 300001`, preflight and Task creation have already succeeded and the evidence sink has acquired its lock, but `controller.run()` throws to the unhandled top level, leaving no finalized `result.json` and a stale evidence lock. Enforce the controller's `0`–`300000` range during argument parsing before the Evidence session is created.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Wait for a stable GUI state in readiness runs**

The readiness scenario navigates and immediately captures without any `gui.wait` step. Because the Playwright launch path only waits for `domcontentloaded` and navigation to the already loaded base URL is a no-op, the final healthy-diagnostics snapshot can occur before OpenChamber's asynchronous initialization requests and console errors arrive, producing a false green readiness result. Wait for a public, stable OpenChamber UI condition before capturing and applying the diagnostics gate.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Strip credentials from resident service environments**

Both resident services inherit the complete parent environment here, including `GAMEFORGE_RUN_RELAY_TOKEN`, CodeArts credentials, and any configured media-provider secrets. A normally configured shell can therefore unintentionally start an authenticated Relay instead of the promised credential-free dependency, while also exposing unrelated credentials to the vendored OpenChamber process. Construct an allowlisted environment with only required runtime variables such as PATH and the explicitly declared service settings.

`loopbackPort()` still accepts loopback `(redacted)` URLs, but `runUp()` always starts plain HTTP services (`run-relay` and OpenChamber `serve --plain`) on the derived port. In that configuration `testenv:up` prints the HTTPS URL as ready, while `testenv:status` / run preflight will only see TLS handshake failures against the same listener. Please either reject HTTPS management URLs here or add actual TLS serving, and cover the mismatch with a regression test.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject HTTPS URLs for plaintext managed services**

The new loopback-host check still accepts `https:` URLs, but `testenv:up` starts the Relay with the repository's plain `node:http` server and launches OpenChamber with `--plain`; readiness only checks whether the port accepts TCP connections. With `GAMEFORGE_RUN_RELAY_URL=https://127.0.0.1:8787/`, `up` therefore prints that the environment is ready even though `status` and harness requests fail their TLS handshake. Restrict managed URLs to `http:` unless TLS is actually configured.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Allow zero to disable the failure hold**

In a headed run where the caller needs immediate teardown, `--failure-hold-ms 0` is rejected because `boundedInteger` delegates to `positiveInteger`, even though `UiTestController` explicitly accepts zero and treats it as disabling the hold. As a result, the new option cannot suppress the default 30-second delay on failures; parse this setting as a non-negative bounded integer instead.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject misspelled tier options before defaulting**

When the direct CLI is invoked with a misspelled option such as `--teir readiness`, the parser never finds `--tier` and never rejects the unconsumed arguments, so this line silently selects the acceptance tier. The run then creates and submits a real Task to CodeArts instead of performing the intended readiness check, potentially consuming model quota; reject unknown options before applying the acceptance default.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Provide an actionable CodeArts installation remedy**

When the CodeArts probe reports that the client is missing or inaccessible, `testenv:status` presents `bun run codearts` as the fix, but that script invokes the same resolver and throws when no executable exists (`integrations/codearts/executable.ts:29-39`). The suggested command therefore deterministically repeats the reported failure; point users to the actual installation/repair instructions or an actionable `CODEARTS_BIN` setup instead.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Exit the foreground supervisor after external down**

When `bun run testenv:down` is invoked from the second terminal advertised above, it kills the Relay and OpenChamber listener children directly, but the original `testenv:up` process remains blocked forever on this never-settling promise because the supervisor does not react to child exits after readiness. The environment's ports are stopped, yet the owning terminal and Bun process leak and a later `up` can create another environment beside the stale owner; monitor the resident children and let the foreground command terminate when they are externally stopped.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

When the direct CLI is invoked with a misspelled flag such as `--teir readiness`, `optionalValue(args, "--tier")` returns `undefined` and this silently defaults to `acceptance`. On a machine with the environment up, that means the caller intended a readiness check but we create/submit a real Task instead, consuming model quota and changing the cost boundary. Please reject unknown/unconsumed `--*` arguments before applying defaults, and add a regression test for the misspelled-tier case.

After `bun run testenv:down` stops the relay/OpenChamber listeners from a second terminal, the original `testenv:up` process is still parked on this never-settling promise. That leaves the advertised foreground owner hanging forever even though the environment is already gone, and a later `up` can create another resident environment beside the stale owner. Please watch the managed children (or otherwise coordinate with external `down`) so the foreground command exits once its services have been stopped externally, and cover that contract with a regression test.

That turns an intended readiness check into a real Task submission, which expands the cost/mutation boundary by consuming model quota and writing Authority state. Please reject unknown or unconsumed `--*` arguments before applying defaults, and add a regression test for the misspelled-tier path.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject URL components discarded during service startup**

When either managed URL uses a currently accepted IPv6 host or non-root base path, this helper validates the URL but returns only its port. For example, `http://[::1]:8787/` starts the Relay on `127.0.0.1` (`packages/run-relay/src/index.ts:7`), while `http://127.0.0.1:8787/relay/` starts a root-mounted Relay but makes preflight request `/relay/tasks`; in both cases `testenv:up` can report TCP readiness although the printed URL and subsequent status/run probes cannot reach the managed service. Restrict managed URLs to the address and root path actually served, or propagate those components into startup and readiness checks.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include evidence finalization in the reported run duration**

Whenever final lifecycle recording or `evidence.finalize()` is slow—for example while consolidating a large MCP audit—`markPhase("teardown")` runs before either operation, so the persisted phase total and `--soft-budget-ms` warning omit that elapsed time even though the CLI is still blocked. This makes the new timing report unable to identify finalization as the slow phase and can report a run as within budget when its actual wall time is not; keep timing through finalization or report that work as a separate phase.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate OpenChamber URLs before running preflight**

When `--openchamber-url` or `GAMEFORGE_OPENCHAMBER_URL` names a non-loopback or credential-bearing URL, this preflight fetches it before `PlaywrightOpenChamberDriver.launch()` applies `safeLoopbackUrl`. A remote page containing the expected OpenChamber markers can therefore pass preflight and cause a real Relay Task to be created, only for browser launch to reject the same URL afterward; even a nonmatching page still receives an unintended outbound request. Apply the driver's credential-free loopback validation during argument parsing, before any probe or Task correlation.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Probe the configured CodeArts attach server before creating a Task**

When the run uses `--codearts-server-url` and `--codearts-session`, the configured server is a required dependency, but this probe set checks only the local client executable, Relay, and OpenChamber. If that loopback CodeArts server is stopped or the session endpoint is unavailable, preflight still passes and the CLI creates a real Task before the attach TUI fails or times out, contrary to the new preflight boundary that missing run dependencies fail before Task correlation. Include an attach-server/session reachability probe whenever attach mode is configured.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require the TUI to remain live through readiness capture**

In a readiness run, CodeArts can reach the initial prompt and then exit or fail while the GUI is mounting; this final `capture` records the TUI's `exited`/`failed` status, but the controller checks only its session ID and still returns `completed` when GUI diagnostics are clean. Acceptance normally catches such an exit through the Authority wait, but readiness has no equivalent gate, so it can produce a green environment verdict whose own Evidence says the real CodeArts client is dead. Require a `running` TUI status at the readiness capture (and fail on an exited client).

Please run the same credential-free loopback validation during argument parsing so unsafe URLs fail before any probe or Task correlation.

Please include an attach reachability probe whenever attach mode is configured (and add a regression test for it).

When `PlaywrightOpenChamberDriver.launch()` fails—for example because Chrome is unavailable—it rolls back its browser resources before rejecting, but `guiLaunched` was already set to true on line 122. This condition consequently waits the default 30 seconds even though no GUI window remains for the operator to inspect; track successful launch/visibility separately from cleanup ownership before applying the failure hold.

When the scenario succeeds but the final `success` snapshot discovers console, page, or request errors, that health check runs later on line 168, outside this catch block. The run therefore skips both `onFailureObserved` and `failureHoldMs` and immediately closes the headed windows, despite final browser diagnostics being a normal failure path that the new hold and pre-teardown guidance are intended to expose.

After the new preflight-specific classifier, this generic rule still treats every `fetch failed` or `ECONNREFUSED` as an Authority Relay outage. For example, `PlaywrightOpenChamberDriver.#remote()` uses `fetch`, so a browser helper that exits after launch produces `fetch failed` and is diagnosed with the unrelated Relay remedy; classify by operation/dependency context rather than matching transport text globally.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Wire OpenChamber to the attached CodeArts session**

The previously verified flow records those steps as necessary in `experiments/2026-07-24-codearts-business-sse/result.md:124-130`; without them, OpenChamber can show its own/default OpenCode state and produce a clean screenshot unrelated to the CodeArts session whose Relay Task completed, invalidating the acceptance evidence.
